program: Sexual assault trauma therapy, advocacy and prevention
priceScope: Matched FY2024 full recipient annual cost against partial individual-therapy benefits, not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift effectiveness.

what: The Blue Bench provides free trauma-specific therapy and advocacy for survivors of sexual assault.
The matched 2024 reference uses 212 individual-therapy clients, not 2,295 mixed service contacts.
Health and signed household resources are assessed together without interpreting uncontrolled symptom improvement as causal QALYs.
strengths: Annual therapy count and full IRS costs are matched to 2024.
Free, time-limited specialist care offers a concrete access mechanism.
Calls, repeated advocacy and overlapping group clients are not added as unique therapy beneficiaries.
reservations: Completion, response, utility, household deduplication and local share remain judgments.
The observed PTSD pre/post comparison lacks a control and does not measure QALYs.
Full recipient costs fund other unquantified channels; current donor capacity is uncertain.

sections.what: Current services include individual and group trauma therapy, crisis support, hospital advocacy, case management and prevention. Therapy does not bill insurance and is usually time-limited to six months. Advocacy or compensation applications do not establish increased disposable income.
sections.monitoring: Request unique therapy clients and households, completed sessions, comparative symptom and utility outcomes, residence inside the pinned ten-county CBSA, actual otherwise-paid copays and after-cost work resources. Separate crisis contacts, advocacy and prevention outcomes from overlapping therapy clients.
sections.qualitative: The annual table sums individual therapy 212, group 40, case management 252, post-conviction advocacy 166, resource navigation 425 and 1,200 calls to a mixed-unit total of 2,295. Only the individual-therapy envelope is used. The reported 76.2% to 25% PTSD symptom criterion comparison is uncontrolled and has unclear sample and attrition; it cannot identify causal utility.
sections.cost: Matched calendar FY2024 full cost is $2,589,919: functional $2,585,426 plus netted direct event $4,493. The observed individual-therapy envelope is 212. Household conversion .9, completion .8, additionality .4, response .4, utility .03 for half a year and local share .95 are judgments. A $200 net household work/resource gain is after tax, benefit withdrawal and work/childcare costs, requires completed eligible care and separate .5 success, and is not survivor gross wages. Positive gains receive .5 overlap adjustment. All exposed households retain full $20 access/time loss and .0002 process harm even with failed benefits. Actual otherwise-paid copay saving and payer loss are central zero judgments, not measured absence. Sensitivities assess full provider/payer losses and unrecognized volunteer opportunity resources. The $1,396,328 therapy/advocacy program cost is a mixed-channel recognized-cost sensitivity, not allocated therapy-only or marginal gift cost.
sections.funding: Own current donation page identifies EIN 84-0905184; no transaction was made. Public victim support, insurance and alternative trauma providers remain in the counterfactual. Current funding disruption and the available newer impact report do not prove funded incremental clinical capacity. Government compensation transfers require recipient and payer incidence, not gross awards as income.

model.costScope: FY2024 full IRS functional cost plus netted direct event expense. Partial individual-therapy benefits; crisis, advocacy, prevention and other benefits unknown, not zero.
model.geographicAttribution: Judged .95 Denver CBSA19740 resident share; nine service counties include Lincoln outside the ten-county pinned boundary. Service catchment does not measure recipient residence.
model.formula: Health = (N × unique × b × eligible × completion × response × q × finite discounted duration − full exposed harm) × local share. Eligible completed changed households jointly log net resources and full access costs; other exposed households retain costs. Distinct payer incidence is localized once. Price = 10 × C / combined health and income equivalents.
model.counterfactual: Other trauma clinicians, public victim support, insurance and natural recovery without this free specialist therapy; untreated access barriers remain plausible.
model.attribution: Additionality .4, completion .8 and response .4 are judgments. Uncontrolled local pre/post symptoms do not identify incremental causal success.
model.uncertainty: Current donor capacity, therapy completion, utility, duration, household overlap, net work gains, provider losses and local residence are unmeasured. Other channels are unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: 2024 annual table reports 212 individual-therapy clients. Group 40 can overlap; mixed total 2,295 includes 1,200 calls and is not unique people or completed households.
